title: Read replicas
idea: A read replica is a read-only copy of your database that serves reads. All writes go to the primary, which copies each change to its replicas.

analogy.text: A head office keeps the master price list. Branches keep photocopies for customers to read; a new price reaches them only after a copy is sent.
analogy.breaks: Databases copy changes automatically and continuously, not by hand.

points: All writes go to the primary, the one database that accepts them.
The primary sends each change to its read-only replicas.
Reads can go to any replica, so read capacity grows with each one.
Copying takes time, so a replica can return old data. This is replication lag.

hero.title: Writes to the primary, reads from replicas

steps.caption: All three databases hold the same data. One user's name is `Ann`.
The user changes the name to `Ada`. The write goes to the primary only.
The primary sends the change on. Replica 1 has it; replica 2 does not yet.
A read that lands on replica 2 now returns the old name. That is replication lag.
The change reaches replica 2. Reads agree again, until the next write.
When a user must see their own write, read that data from the primary.

code.title: Replication lag, in code
code.caption: A write lands on the primary first. The replica sees it only after `replicate()` runs.

pitfalls: Do not read from a replica right after a write when the user must see it.
Replicas do not speed up writes: every write still goes to the primary.
Watch replication lag; a replica that falls behind serves stale data.

quiz.q: Which two values does the snippet print, in order?
quiz.why: The write reaches only the primary. The replica gets it when `replicate()` runs, so the first read is `undefined`.

takeaway: Replicas add read capacity, not write capacity, and can lag behind.
